pillar_reactions.evidence: Brady engaged lightly at first — 'Can you commit to three to four times per week, 30 minutes per session?' / '100% man' and 'I just want to take instruction' — and volunteered his own practice ('I do use, like, foam rollers and lacrosse balls and things for deep tissue myofascial release... I'm pretty tight in my hips'). The real interrogation came from his wife once she joined: 'with the mobility, is there like a specific like philosophy that Trevor likes to follow, as far as like chain of connections, or is this like fascia-based?... Because people will say mobility, but it's like, is that just simple stretching?' Also 'is there like a graduation from the program?' and whether mobility stays foundational throughout. Understanding-seeking at a level no other prospect in this batch reached.

Volunteered a positive reaction to the fasting content — 'Fully believe in that, man. Good stuff, man' — and then gave the household's whole regime unprompted: 'we definitely stick to a whole foods diet and try to do majority of it, like, 90% of it organic. Like, we read all the labels, we keep all the PUFAs out, like, the oils, and we've been doing this for almost a decade. It's not a trend, it's not a trend for us, it's a lifestyle.' His wife works with individuals on biophysiology. The rep read it correctly: 'it's going to make the job easy for us as well.'

He pre-sold himself on this pillar twenty minutes before it was presented, and tied it directly to his own track record: 'And I need a community too. Like, the best that I've ever been in the past when it comes to working out or anything like that was always in a setting where it was, like, camaraderie or team driven, you know, because I just need the accountability, honestly.' Then: 'the times that I plug into a community, I excel and I become one of the best.' He also volunteered the structural need — 'I need a team that I can plug into or accountability. So I know that that's a missing link.'

anchors.raw: I'm not comfortable with doing a credit card. I literally just wiped out a lot of credit card debt, and I don't want to pay 20 some odd percent interest fees.
anchors.note: The most consequential anchor on the call. He set an explicit ceiling on the cost of borrowing at around 20% and was then routed into a financing plan totalling $7,800 on a $6,000 programme, roughly 30%, described to him as 'just a little bit of interest on top. Yeah, it's nothing crazy there.'

anchors.raw: Between Elbow and Truck, we're paying like $700 a month... I need my bottom line that I need to make every month before I have any extra funds is, like, $7,800. So adding that $650 would make it to where we're closer to $8,500 minimum.
anchors.note: A precise, quantified affordability picture volunteered without resistance. He named $250/month as the figure that would not strain the household. The close landed at $650/month, 2.6 times his stated ceiling, bridged on a future contract payment.

anchors.raw: I have a big contract that I just signed for a full home renovation... my net take-home should be $31,000. That will help me, obviously, to pay down the plan.
anchors.note: The rep built the entire close on this — 'if we know that we're getting that significant chunk of change in one go, pretty much in what, six weeks... Why not get started in this moment?' The prospect himself flagged the risk in it: construction projects get delayed and 'the profit margin isn't always exact because there's things that come up on a project that were unforeseen.'

anchors.raw: I didn't expect six grand. I didn't expect for it to be $100 either, right? In order to create something tailored to me specifically, there has to be time put into it that you guys should be paid, you know, a good amount. When I do restoration or renovation projects, I'm typically not the cheapest, I'm not the most expensive, but I give a quality product.
anchors.note: He justified the price to himself using his own contracting business as the analogy, unprompted, seconds after hearing it. As strong a value anchor as appears anywhere in this batch — a buyer who prices bespoke work for a living and accepts the logic.

anchors.raw: We've done, you know, traditional, like, CrossFit and weightlifting and all that kind of stuff, but where we're at now, like, with our understanding of the human body and, like, dynamics and how we're, like, actually supposed to move... I told him, like, if he was going to start training, like, I wanted him to start training in a way that was more fluid and dynamic
anchors.note: The wife had independently arrived at the programme's positioning before the call and had already ruled out the heavy-loaded alternatives. She was the strongest advocate in the room by the end, which is why the OB play resolved rather than stalled.

unmet_demand.want: Programming designed by someone with rehabilitation credentials, for a client six weeks post-surgery and not yet cleared — his wife asked outright, 'Do you guys like have people on staff that like incorporate in the programming?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The answer contained no clear yes or no on credentials, and the method described was symptom-guided self-report: 'he would basically just tell Brady like this is what I think would be suit best if it feels good for you continue with it if it doesn't then he will switch it out for something else.' The programme is not clinically supervised rehabilitation and the prospect already has a treating physical therapist nobody proposed coordinating with.

unmet_demand.want: A monthly payment at or near $250, the figure he named as safe for the household
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The lowest available structure was $650/month over 12 months. Nothing in the offer reaches his stated ceiling, and no deferred start was proposed even though he had a known $31,000 inflow six weeks out and had himself suggested waiting for it.

unmet_demand.want: Something useful to do in the two to three weeks before he is cleared — 'if there is anything I could be doing, I would like to know'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered by pointing at the Skool community rather than with any guidance on what is safe pre-clearance. He was instead booked into a Trevor kickoff two days later at which 'he may ask you to do a few initial movement patterns live in front of the camera', which falls before his clearance date.
